ai.definition: Satellites for Earth observation are spacecraft equipped with various sensors to collect detailed images and data about the Earth's surface and atmosphere. These satellites can provide high-resolution imagery and precise measurements of environmental conditions.
ai.howItWorks: These satellites use multi-spectral sensors, which capture data across different wavelengths of light, including visible, near-infrared, thermal infrared, and microwave bands. Advanced communication systems transmit this data back to ground stations for processing and analysis.
ai.problemSolved: They address the need for continuous and detailed monitoring of environmental changes, natural disasters, agricultural productivity, urban planning, and more. This enables better decision-making in various fields such as climate change research, resource management, and emergency response.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process involves designing and building the satellite platform, integrating sensors and communication systems, testing for performance and reliability, and launching into orbit. Each component is carefully selected to ensure the satellite can operate effectively in space.
ai.buildProcess: Satellites are typically built by specialized aerospace companies or research institutions. The build process includes detailed design, component integration, rigorous testing, and final assembly before launch preparation.
ai.costDrivers: Cost drivers include the complexity of the satellite design, the type and number of sensors, the spacecraft's size and weight, launch costs, and the need for long-term maintenance and support.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook is positive as demand continues to grow with advancements in technology and increasing awareness of environmental issues. However, there are challenges related to cost and regulatory compliance.
ai.regulation: Regulations vary by country but generally involve licensing for launch, operation, and data sharing. International agreements also govern the use of space and satellite communications.
ai.risks: Risks include technical failures during launch or in orbit, cybersecurity threats, and geopolitical tensions that can affect access to space resources.
ai.profitability: Profitability is variable depending on the specific application and market segment. High-value applications like precision agriculture or oil exploration may offer better returns than more general environmental monitoring services.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future developments could include smaller, cheaper satellites for constellations that provide even higher resolution data; improved sensor technology for real-time data collection; and enhanced communication systems for faster data transmission.

glossary.def: Sensors that can capture images or measurements across multiple wavelengths of light, providing detailed information about the Earth's surface and atmosphere.
A group of satellites designed to work together in a coordinated manner, often used for continuous coverage and improved data collection capabilities.

subsystems.name: Platform (bus)
subsystems.role: the structural and thermal backbone that keeps every instrument at the right temperature and pointing correctly.

subsystems.name: Power
subsystems.role: generates and stores electricity for the payload and housekeeping systems.

subsystems.name: Attitude and orbit control
subsystems.role: measures and controls the satellite's orientation and orbit to keep the camera or radar aimed at the target.

subsystems.name: Payload
subsystems.role: the actual sensing instrument that collects the data.
parts: radar antenna and transmitter (synthetic aperture radar)

subsystems.name: Communications
subsystems.role: sends the captured data to ground and receives commands.

subsystems.name: Ground segment
subsystems.role: receives, processes and distributes the imagery and measurements.

buildSteps.title: Define the mission and orbit
buildSteps.detail: Choose what to observe, how often, and at what resolution. That sets the orbit: Sun-synchronous for consistent lighting, geostationary for continuous coverage, or a lower inclination for specific latitudes.

buildSteps.title: Design and fabricate the bus
buildSteps.detail: Engineers lay out structure, power, thermal control and propulsion to fit the payload's mass, power and pointing needs.

buildSteps.title: Build the instrument
buildSteps.detail: Optics are ground and polished, detectors are bonded to focal planes, and the whole assembly is aligned to micron tolerances in a clean room.

buildSteps.title: Integrate payload with the bus
buildSteps.detail: The instrument is mechanically and electrically mated to the satellite, then tested as a single system.

buildSteps.title: Environmental testing
buildSteps.detail: The satellite is shaken on a vibration table, baked in a thermal vacuum chamber to simulate space, and checked for electromagnetic compatibility.

buildSteps.title: Launch and deploy
buildSteps.detail: It is encapsulated in a fairing, launched to its orbit, and its solar arrays and antennas unfurl.

buildSteps.title: Commissioning
buildSteps.detail: Over the first weeks or months, each subsystem is switched on, the instrument is calibrated against known ground targets, and the orbit is fine-tuned.

buildSteps.title: Operations and data delivery
buildSteps.detail: The satellite is tasked daily, downlinks its data, and the ground segment turns raw signals into calibrated images and maps for users.

prerequisites.tech: Worldwide ground station network and data pipelines
prerequisites.why: turn a stream of raw bits into timely, usable information for forecasters and responders.

pathway.milestone: operational programmes such as Landsat and Copernicus provide decades-long records of land, ice and oceans
pathway.unlocks: climate monitoring, forestry, agriculture and disaster mapping at global scale.

pathway.milestone: constellations of small satellites give daily or sub-daily revisit over any point
pathway.unlocks: near-real-time tracking of floods, fires and crop stress.

pathway.milestone: on-board AI filters images and sends only alerts, not raw data
pathway.unlocks: faster warnings when downlink bandwidth is limited.

pathway.milestone: integrated digital models that fuse satellite data with ground sensors and weather models
pathway.unlocks: predictive management of resources and hazards, from water to wildfires.
